The parent OB=64 is at the bf16 edge. CONCLUSION on the widen-OB lever: blocked by bf16 factor gate. Pivoting to: (a) remove the per-call _n352_illcond_mask .any() D2H sync (always-False on the dense scored shape), (b) panel cmf-warps occupancy, (c) the n176 megakernel latency. A. MULTI-CTA-PER-MATRIX for the n176 megakernel + n352 panel: split each matrix's trailing-column apply across 2-4 CTAs (the apply is embarrassingly parallel across columns) to use the idle SMs -- but the panel/reflector chain is serial and the matrix is smem-resident, so this needs a global-memory blocked QR with inter-CTA sync per column (which historically lost to the megakernel; worth re-measuring now that the megakernel is only 17% SM-busy).

CholeskyQR for n176/n352 (G=A^T A + batched potrf + R-solve + orhr_col recon): turns the serial Householder chain into batched GEMMs that saturate all 148 SMs at B=40 -- BUT it squares cond(A) and the orhr_col recon is exactly the gate-riding pattern that broke brief-4 remotely, so it needs an ill-cond guard + a tight margin check.

D. 2-matrices-per-CTA with PER-MATRIX named barriers (not __syncthreads) so one matrix's serial-chain stall is hidden by the other's work -- deep rewrite; note worker on brief-7 is testing a 2mat variant on n512 (saw their profile), may inform this.
Recommend NOT spending more workers on graph capture or OB-widening (both proven dead). So 'fill the idle SMs with GEMM-trailing' loses at n176; residence+single-fused-launch wins even at 17% SM-busy. The coordinator's 2.5x-on-s1 premise (trailing dominates) is contradicted by measurement. Reverting to clean+hoist deliverable. ROOT CAUSE (both small shapes): the bottleneck is the PER-MATRIX SERIAL HOUSEHOLDER PANEL on 40 CTAs (B=40). It (a) cannot be split across CTAs -- each reflector depends on the prior (strict serial); the mega already does 1-sync/column look-ahead = the algorithmic floor; (b) cannot gain occupancy -- 40<148 SMs and the look-ahead design is 1 CTA/SM. The trailing (the only parallel part) is already optimal: resident for n176, batched GEMM for n352. 'Fill idle SMs' targets the trailing, which is not where the time is.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY MOVE IT (all are NEW algorithms with remote-precision risk, none is a trailing-parallelism tweak):
- CholeskyQR for n176/n352: replaces the serial panel ENTIRELY with G=A^T A (one batched GEMM, all SMs) + batched potrf + orhr_col recon. This attacks the PANEL (the real bottleneck), not the trailing. BUT it squares cond(A) and orhr_col is exactly the gate-rider that broke brief-4 remotely -- needs an ill-cond guard + held-out margin gate. This is the only thing that could get the 2x, and it must be a fresh macro brief with heavy numerical validation.
- 2-matrices-per-CTA: brief-7 measured -2.5% at n512; HALVES CTA count (40->20) so it makes the under-filled small shapes' SM coverage WORSE. Ruled out.
- Lower-precision panel (FP16/bf16 reflectors at n176): measured NO-GO historically (orth collapses at n>=176).

RECOMMENDATION: stop pointing workers at trailing-parallelism / fill-idle-SMs for the small shapes -- 3 independent measurements (trial-8 n176 GEMM-trailing +62%, trial-5 n352 PAF +26%, the n352 profile showing panel=65%) prove the trailing is not the bottleneck. The serial panel is the wall. The ONLY path to the geomean prize is replacing the panel algorithm (CholeskyQR), which is a precision-risky macro brief, not an occupancy tweak. The dispatch-hoist deliverable is the safe, neutral, remote-valid result; the small shapes are at their floor for any Householder-panel design.
